title: Importer ignores vanilla [General] PrerequisitePower/Factory/Barracks/Radar/Tech/Proc; generic prereqs become unreachable literal ids
description: ParseGenericPrerequisites only reads a [GenericPrerequisites] section. That section comes from the Ares extension. Vanilla RA2/YR rulesmd.ini defines the generic groups as [General] PrerequisitePower=, PrerequisiteFactory=, PrerequisiteBarracks=, PrerequisiteRadar=, PrerequisiteTech= and PrerequisiteProc=. On a vanilla file every POWER, FACTORY, etc. token turns into a singleton group ["POWER"] that names no unit, so almost the whole tech tree becomes unbuildable.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a scratch program. INI has [General] PrerequisitePower=GAPOWR,NAPOWR and PrerequisiteFactory=GAWEAP,NAWEAP; GAPILE has Prerequisite=POWER and MTNK has Prerequisite=FACTORY. Import gives GAPILE pre=[POWER] and MTNK pre=[FACTORY]. CanBuild(Allied,{GACNST,GAPOWR},GAPILE) returns False, and PathTo(Allied,{GACNST},MTNK) returns null. Any playbook tech goal would be reported as unreachable.
suggested_fix: Also read [General] Prerequisite{Power,Factory,Barracks,Radar,Tech,Proc} and map them to POWER/FACTORY/BARRACKS/RADAR/TECH/PROC, with [GenericPrerequisites] (Ares) taking precedence when present. Add an importer test that uses the vanilla layout.

title: Verses= parsed with wrong armor order, so tanks classify as AntiStructure and get role Support
description: ClassifyByVerses assumes the order [none, wood, light, heavy, concrete, ...]. RA2/YR Verses order is none, flak, plate, light, medium, heavy, wood, steel, concrete, special_1, special_2. The 'infantry' average therefore reads none+flak, the 'armor' average reads plate+light, and 'structure' reads the medium entry. AntiStructure has no non-building role mapping, so a main battle tank ends up as UnitRole.Support. The composition planner then never counts or builds it as anti-armor.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. AP warhead Verses=25%,25%,25%,90%,75%,75%,70%,40%,40%,100%,100% (weak vs infantry, strong vs light/medium/heavy, weak vs concrete). The imported MTNK gets weapon=AntiStructure, role=Support. It should be AntiArmor/AntiArmor.
suggested_fix: Index Verses by the real RA2 armor order (0 none, 1 flak, 2 plate, 3 light, 4 medium, 5 heavy, 6 wood, 7 steel, 8 concrete, 9/10 special). Average infantry-like entries (none, flak, plate), vehicle entries (light, medium, heavy) and structure entries (wood, steel, concrete). Map AntiStructure units to a role (e.g. Artillery or Support) on purpose.

title: Anti-air detection reads AA= on the weapon/unit, but RA2 keeps AA= on the Projectile; Secondary is ignored
description: explicitAntiAir checks GetBool(weapon,"AA") || GetBool(unit,"AA"). In rulesmd, AA=yes/AG=no live on the weapon's Projectile= section. As a result no real AA weapon is ever detected. title: PathTo keeps buildings from a failed alternative in the returned plan
description: TryAdd(candidate) calls TryResolve, which appends the candidate's sub-prerequisites to plan/trial as it goes. When a later group of that candidate fails, TryAdd returns false but never rolls back plan or trial. The resolver then tries the next alternative, and the returned 'shortest path' still contains buildings that only the abandoned alternative needed. OperationalPlanner.FirstStepToward takes the first unowned step, so the bot spends money on the useless building first.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. GOAL needs CHEAP|DEAR. CHEAP (100, cheaper) needs POW and SOVONLY (Soviet-only, so not eligible for Allied). DEAR needs only YARD. PathTo(Allied,{YARD},GOAL) returns [POW, DEAR]; the correct answer is [DEAR]. POW is built first for nothing.
suggested_fix: Snapshot plan.Count and a copy of trial (or record the additions) before each candidate attempt, and restore both when the attempt fails.
verification: RulesDatabase.cs:181-186: `bool ok = TryResolve(candidate, ...); resolving.Remove(...); if (!ok) return false; plan.Add(candidate.TypeId); trial.Add(candidate.TypeId);`. The nested TryResolve call has already run TryAdd on earlier groups, and TryAdd appends to plan/trial with no snapshot or restore. Lines 163-170 then try the next candidate against the modified plan/trial. PathTo line 99: `return TryResolve(rule, faction, trial, plan, []) ? plan : null;` returns the plan as-is. Nothing rolls back the entries anywhere. | src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Rules/RulesDatabase.cs:163-170 is the outer loop: a candidate that fails is skipped, and nothing is restored. Lines 176-188 are TryAdd: `bool ok = TryResolve(...); resolving.Remove(...); if (!ok) return false;`. Here only `resolving` is restored. `plan` and `trial` keep the prerequisites the nested TryAdd calls already appended (lines 185-186). PathTo, lines 92-99, returns `plan` as is. Callers: src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Operations/OperationalPlanner.cs:232, src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Arbitration/IntentValidator.cs:296, and src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Claude/IntentPromptBuilder.cs:165,193. `git status --short` printed nothing. | src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Rules/RulesDatabase.cs lines 161-171: `foreach (UnitRule candidate in candidates) { if (TryAdd(...)) { satisfied = true; break; } } if (!satisfied) return false;` There is no snapshot or restore of plan or trial around each attempt. title: Prerequisite tokens and type ids are case-sensitive, although INI sections are matched case-insensitively

title: Naval=yes buildings (shipyard) become EntityKind.Naval / QueueKind.Naval and lose Production role
description: The Naval flag is applied to every kind, including BuildingTypes. A shipyard that carries Naval=yes becomes Kind=Naval and Queue=Naval. InferRole then takes the non-building branch (role Support instead of Production). The sim's OwnedBuildingTypes (Kind==Building) and planner FirstStepToward (Queue==Building) also stop treating it as a building, so naval units behind it are unreachable.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. [GAYARD] Naval=yes, WaterBound=yes, Factory=UnitType imports as kind=Naval, role=Support, q=Naval. FirstStepToward returns null for it, so it is never built, and a placed yard is not counted as an owned building for naval-unit prerequisites.
suggested_fix: Apply the Naval kind/queue override only for VehicleTypes. For BuildingTypes keep Kind=Building and Queue=Building.

title: Playbook parameters the LLM is asked to tune (harassIntervalSeconds, siegeRangeBufferCells, defendThreatRatio) have no effect
description: Build-sequence step 5 has the LLM select and parameterize validated playbooks. Nothing in src or tools reads harassIntervalSeconds (allied-harass), siegeRangeBufferCells (soviet-v3-siege) or defendThreatRatio (generic-defend). defendThreatRatio exists only as a PinnedPlaybookStrategist constructor argument, not as an intent parameter. harvesterTarget is described as the harvester count to reach before committing to the push, but the planner uses it only as a harvester production target and never gates the attack on it. suggested_fix: Either implement the parameters in the operational and tactical layers (harass sortie timer, siege standoff distance in SquadController targeting, defend-recall threshold in the planner) or remove them from the playbooks, so the validator and prompt stop advertising them.
